Definition: from G3624 and the base of G3551; a house-distributor (i.e. manager), or overseer, i.e. an employee in that capacity; by extension, a fiscal agent (treasurer); figuratively, a preacher (of the Gospel):--chamberlain, governor, steward.
BiblicalUsage: Oikonomos is a steward, the house manager, the overseer of the estate. Jesus asks who the faithful and wise steward is in Luke 12:42, the one set over the household to give food in due season, and Paul calls himself and his fellow workers stewards of the mysteries of God in 1 Corinthians 4:1. Erastus the chamberlain is greeted in Romans 16:23, and Galatians 4:2 puts the heir under stewards until the time appointed by the father.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a steward is judged by faithfulness, not by ownership, because the house was never his. My position is that the mysteries of God are the steward's charge, and the faithful steward hands them on whole.
